title: Pide sucuklu
subtitle: Turkish flatbread with spiced sausage and mozzarella
excerpt: Pide sucuklu are boat-shaped Turkish flatbreads filled with spiced merguez sausage, mozzarella, and tomato paste, baked at high heat until the bread is golden and the cheese is bubbling. Merguez gives a similar spiced-lamb character to the Turkish sucuk it replaces.
sourceNotes: Aylin Oney Tan, A Taste of Sun and Fire: Gaziantep Cookery (2014). Sucuklu pide documented as one of the most popular pide varieties at Turkish pideci shops. Paula Wolfert, The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean (1994). Turkish pide dough and the sucuk filling described.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dough can prove overnight in the fridge. Bring to room temperature before shaping.
recipe.temperatureNote: Fan 220 degrees / gas 9. Preheat for 30 minutes.

content.text: Sucuklu pide are Turkish flatbread boats filled with sliced spiced sausage, mozzarella, and tomato paste, baked in a very hot oven until the bread is crisp and the filling is deeply browned and molten. The sucuk (Turkish beef sausage) is replaced here with merguez, which has a similar spiced-lamb quality. Eat immediately while the cheese is still pulling and the bread is hot.

items.prepNote: sliced into 1 cm rounds (substitute for sucuk)

content.text: Mix {{yeast-dried}} and {{caster-sugar}} into 260 ml of warm water. Leave for five minutes. Combine {{strong-bread-flour}} and {{sea-salt-fine}}. Add the yeast mixture and {{olive-oil}}, mix, and knead for eight minutes. Cover and prove for one hour until doubled.

Preheat the oven to 240 degrees. Divide the dough into four pieces. On a floured surface, roll each piece into an oval about 30 cm long and 15 cm wide. Pinch the ends into points and roll the edges up slightly.
Brush the inside of each boat with the diluted {{tomato-puree}}. Scatter {{mozzarella}} inside, then lay {{merguez}} slices over the top. Season with {{black-pepper}} and {{chilli-flakes}} if using.
Lay the pide on preheated baking trays. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the edges are golden, the base is cooked through, and the cheese is bubbling and browned. Eat immediately.

items.symptom: The merguez is releasing a lot of fat
items.fix: Blot the sausage slices with kitchen paper after slicing to remove some surface fat before adding to the pide.

items.symptom: The base is raw in the middle
items.fix: Pide requires a fully preheated oven at 240 degrees. Preheat for at least 30 minutes and put the trays in with the oven.

items.symptom: The edges don't hold their boat shape
items.cause: Dough rolled too thin or not pinched firmly
items.fix: Pinch the ends firmly and roll the edges up by at least 1 cm. Let the shaped pide rest for five minutes before topping.

items.cause: Fresh mozzarella in brine releases liquid when heated
items.fix: Tear the mozzarella and leave on kitchen paper for 20 minutes before using to drain excess moisture.

content.text: Sucuklu pide is one of the top sellers at pideci shops across Turkey. The combination of spiced sausage, melted cheese, and bread is popular everywhere, and it sits alongside sucuklu yumurta as one of the main ways Turkish sucuk features in daily cooking. Sucuk is a cured sausage that keeps well: sold in rings and stable at room temperature for weeks. The flavour is garlicky and cumin-forward, quite different from any European cured sausage. Merguez is the best available substitute, though the garlic note in sucuk is stronger.
